nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Quantile regression was used to obtain a normative range of regional CTh variation (5th and 95th percentiles) as a function of age and sex.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: Quantile regression [8] was used to obtain a normative range of regional CTh variation [2] based on the following model... Bootstrapping was used to estimate confidence intervals for the 5% and 95% percentiles of regional CTh variation.

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: Regional cortical thickness (CTh) estimated for 34 cortical regions (left hemisphere) of the Desikan-Killiany atlas.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: To characterize CTh heterogeneity, normative ranges (i.e., centiles) in regional CTh [3, 12, 13] were deﬁned on healthy controls as a function of age and sex, and CTh deviations were then estimated for each individual with schizophrenia.

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: The normative model included sex, age, sex-by-age interaction, and quadratic age effects as predictors.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: beta_1 is the between-sex difference in CTh at age A , beta_2 is the rate at which CTh changes per year at age A , while beta_3 and beta_4 model the sex-by-age interaction and quadratic age effects, respectively.
